sections_in_order: Medical Records Documentation Used for Review
criteria_location: Coverage Rationale, pp.1-3 only (about 2.5 pages of 18); Definitions pp.3-6 carry the numeric severity tables (FEV1 bands, OSA severity). Daytime studies (MSLT) are delegated to InterQual.
procedures_covered: PSG for other conditions (PLMD, RLS, parasomnia, narcolepsy, CSA)
Not medically necessary: PSG for circadian, depression, insomnia; actigraphy; PAP-Nap

logic.top_level: pathways: HSAT = default for adults with suspected OSA; PSG has any-of list for OSA and a separate any-of list for 'Other Conditions'
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: HSAT contraindications are phrased as positive PSG indications: 'Individual is known to have one or more of the following comorbid medical conditions that prohibits the use of a HSAT' (7 items). Not-medically-necessary studies listed under 'Other Studies'.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: 'Attended Repeat Testing': 'When the above criteria for an attended study are met, repeat attended full-channel Polysomnography and repeat PAP titration are medically necessary' for persistent symptoms despite treatment OR weight change >=10%. Repeat HSAT discouraged by a Note.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Results of previous (within the past 12 months) HSAT are negative or indeterminate to make a diagnosis of OSA ...; or Individual is a child or adolescent ...; or Individual is known to have one or more of the following comorbid
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Bullets are glyph-less in the text extraction; the 'or' is at line ends so list is any-of but visually looks like three separate rules.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Attended full-channel Polysomnography is medically necessary following an appropriate clinical assessment either because OSA has been excluded, OSA has been adequately treated, or documented symptoms suggest one of the following conditions
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Nested: (OSA excluded OR treated OR documented symptoms) wrapped around the condition list; not clear whether the 'either' clause is required for each condition.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Where HSAT is indicated, an autotitrating Positive Airway Pressure (APAP) device is an option
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Permissive; 'indicated' has no criteria - HSAT is simply 'medically necessary for evaluating adults with suspected OSA'.

requirement_kinds.quote: Home Sleep Apnea Testing (HSAT), using a portable monitor, is medically necessary for evaluating adults with suspected Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA).
Results of previous (within the past 12 months) HSAT are negative or indeterminate to make a diagnosis of OSA
Individual is a child or adolescent (i.e., less than 18 years of age)
Significant Chronic Pulmonary Disease as defined by a forced expiratory volume (FEV1) % predicted of < 60%
New York Heart Association class III or IV ... or left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%
Parasomnia with documented disruptive, violent, or potentially injurious sleep behaviors
RLS ... that has not responded to treatment

persistent, recurrent or new symptoms, despite documented appropriate current treatment or PAP therapy (e.g., equipment failure, improper mask fit, pressure leaks, unsuccessful titration, inadequate pressure, and medical problems including nasal congestion have been addressed
clinically significant weight loss or gain (≥ 10%) since the last study
Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria

thresholds.quote: clinically significant weight loss or gain (≥ 10%)
obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) and daytime hypercapnia (arterial PaCO2 ≥ 45 mm Hg)
Adequate HSAT occurs over a minimum of four hours
Mild for AHI or RDI ≥ 5 and < 15

extraction_hazards: Bullets render as private-use glyphs or nothing in pdftotext, so list items have no markers; only indentation and 'or' at line ends show the structure.
Running header/footer ('Sleep Studies Page n of 18', proprietary notice) interrupts the criteria lists mid-bullet-group (p.1->2).
Short criteria section (3 pages) followed by 15 pages of definitions, evidence, references.
Inline literature citations after thresholds (e.g. '(Pellegrino et al., 2005)').
InterQual criteria live behind a hyperlink ('Click here to view the InterQual® criteria'), not in the PDF.
interesting_structures: HSAT is the default; PSG only on exception - the logic is 'HSAT unless ...' with no symptom prerequisites.
Criteria for MSLT delegated wholly to InterQual.
Daytime studies may be done at night 'if necessary to match an individual's normal sleep pattern'.
Table of FEV1 severity bands in Definitions drives the pulmonary threshold.

fit_to_tree.why: Short, mostly any-of lists of comorbidities with numeric cutoffs; the strain is the InterQual delegation for MSLT, 'suspected OSA' undefined, and open-ended 'examples include but are not limited to' lists.
